there's a lot of potential panic about this, quick thoughts:

almost nothing onchain uses RSA directly except for like Arweave (plus some zk-login and MPC custody setups)

the bigger concern would be the speculative but potentially real chain of fast factoring -> broken pairings

now, pairings are used in crypto: curves like BN254 and BLS12-381, and the BLS signatures, Groth16, KZG built on them

mostly for finality but also for certain zk systems (but not all! eg, ironwood in zcash would not be affected, so if you have funds in an ancient pool, migrate them)

to be clear, this is a different panic than the one from a few months ago about standard ECC being cracked

overall:

- this stuff is still highly speculative. even if factoring is in P -- what's the exponent? is an attack even feasible?

- the causal chain of spillover is even more speculative but still credible

- we should be upgrading some of the shakier cryptographic foundations in these systems regardless, as these things will keep advancing

- in the blockchain context, even if factoring + pairings were broken, it'd be bad but not catastrophic vs. ECC being broken and directly draining wallets; so I do not think panic is warranted

trillions

US New Home Sales jumped to a 701K annual rate in October, the most since Dec 2025 and above every estimate in Bloomberg's survey. 

The caveats: It's a one-region story fueled by buyers snapping up the least expensive homes and comes only after a big downward revision to September (this report is very volatile with heavy revisions).

▪️ +14.2% m/m, even with mortgage rates peaking at 7.5% in early Oct, the highest in almost three years (Bloomberg). But Sep was cut to 614K from 676K (now −9.7% m/m), so Oct is only 21K above Aug's 680K. The gain is also inside the Census ±22.6% margin of error. As ZeroHedge put it, "it's anyone's guess where this October rebound ends up."
▪️ South +137K to 515K, the biggest one-month gain on record (data to 1973) and the most since Mar 2021. A record 73.5% of all sales.
▪️ The other three regions combined −21.2% to the lowest since Jul 2022. West joint-lowest since Mar 2014, Northeast lowest since Apr 2015.
▪️ Average price $459.9K, lowest since Jul 2021, −12.1% y/y (steepest drop since Apr 2009). Median $391.3K, −3.2% y/y. Bill McBride puts both 15% below their 2022 peaks.
▪️ Under-$300K homes were 25% of sales, the highest share since 2021 (Bloomberg). Builders are leaning "heavily on costly sales incentives."
▪️ Homes for sale 470K, fewest since Aug 2024. Months' supply 8.0, the least since Dec 2025 but above the 4–6 normal for 56 straight months. Since 2000, the median price was lower a year later 72% of the time at this level.
▪️ Under construction 245K, down 5 straight months to the joint-fewest since Jul 2021. McBride says builders are "probably waiting to start some homes until they clear more inventory."

As ZeroHedge put it, "it's anyone's guess where this October rebound ends up."
▪️ South +137K to 515K, the biggest one-month gain on record (data to 1973) and the most since Mar 2021. A record 73.5% of all sales.
▪️ The other three regions combined −21.2% to the lowest since Jul 2022. West joint-lowest since Mar 2014, Northeast lowest since Apr 2015.
▪️ Average price $459.9K, lowest since Jul 2021, −12.1% y/y (steepest drop since Apr 2009). Median $391.3K, −3.2% y/y. Bill McBride puts both 15% below their 2022 peaks.
▪️ Under-$300K homes were 25% of sales, the highest share since 2021 (Bloomberg). Builders are leaning "heavily on costly sales incentives."
▪️ Homes for sale 470K, fewest since Aug 2024. Months' supply 8.0, the least since Dec 2025 but above the 4–6 normal for 56 straight months. Since 2000, the median price was lower a year later 72% of the time at this level.
▪️ Under construction 245K, down 5 straight months to the joint-fewest since Jul 2021. McBride says builders are "probably waiting to start some homes until they clear more inventory."

Ben Horowitz on why a16z fines its VCs $10 a minute for being late to founder meetings:

"The title of the book comes from the Bushido, which says, 'A culture is not a set of beliefs. It's a set of actions.' And the book is about how do you get the actions to be what you want them to be."

"We wanted to respect the entrepreneurial process and how hard it was, but how do you do that?... If you're late for a meeting with an entrepreneur, you pay a fine, $10 a minute."

"Oh, you had to go to the bathroom? You're five minutes late? Great, $50. Oh, you had a really important business call? You're 10 minutes late, $100. And they're like, 'Ben, why am I paying you to work here? That doesn't seem fair.'"

"I need you to understand how hard it is to build a company, and I need you to understand so much that you plan to be on time. And I know that business call was important. I know you had to go to the bathroom, but if it was your wedding, you wouldn't have been late. So it's got to be that important to you."

The Trump administration's actions to support equity markets at all costs comes at a drastic expense to the lower and middle income citizens and small and medium sized businesses, the exact people who elected him into office for change.

In my view, there is nowhere near the appropriate appreciation amongst the general public and market participants for how these actions hurt the parts of the population and economy who have the least ability to weather the costs. The equity market focused stimulus measures keeps asset values high, the top part of the K-shaped economy healthy and their consumer spending robust. This produces above-trend demand into a supply constrained economy where the lower and middle income class are seeing negative real wages and don't have investment portfolios to draw from and offset that burden. They are falling further and further behind.

These equity market focused stimulus measures are creating inflation and add fuel to the fire burning down the lower and middle class by forcing the Fed to hike interest rates. These front-end interest rate hikes have an outsized negative impact on small businesses while the administration's suppression of long-end yields benefit the wealthy and long-term corporate borrowers.

These are all measures the Trump administration and its top officials (@SecScottBessent et al) campaigned against and vowed to fix, but they continue the same policy path that has led to the most imbalanced and unequal economy and wealth divide in decades.

There's a reason this administration has record low approval ratings and rapidly deteriorating polling numbers going into midterms. They continue to worsen the economic hardship onto the workers least able to bear it and least able to articulate what is happening to them while making the rich richer and ensuring the top 1% and technology oligarchs continue to reap the rewards.

When you truly understand the ramifications of what's happening at the direction of policymakers and elected officials who were voted into office to do the opposite, and assuming you have a human heart and conscious, it's hard not to adopt a "burn it down" view.

the world didn’t end then and it won’t end now

the world didn’t end then and it won’t end now

thread_tweets.text:
unlike many other professions, people who aren’t coders and mathematicians have no idea what coders and mathematicians actually do

when someone is a photographer, other people understand what the photographer does even if they aren’t photographers. they have a rough idea of how it works, and even the meta properties of how the photography field as a whole works, how one becomes a famous photographer, etc

when an ai model figures out how to create photos, it’s actually devastating to the field of photography. the negative impact of that is imo very likely to be much greater than the hypothetical negative impact of any cryptographic assumption being broken

however since we all have an intuitive understanding of the field of photography even if we’re not experts, the theoretical impact, as significant as it is, is BOUNDED. we all know what the worst case is. so while actual photographers are losing their shit, the rest of us generally moved on

coders and math heads aren’t like that, 99% of folks have no idea what those people do. everybody uses cryptography every day yet no one has any idea how it works. therefore the hypothetical impact, in the average person’s mind, is unbounded

are planes going to fall off the sky? will nuclear codes leak leading to atomic bombs going off in major cities? will all bank accounts zero out? well… why not?

the people whose job it is to calm people down are too preoccupied in the same existential crisis photographers already went through. they’re too busy asking themselves “who am i” to consider that planes aren’t going to fall out of the sky actually

————

if it makes you feel better: cryptography is a tool. society does not run on cryptography. society runs on humans. and humans figure shit out. even if photography breaks or cryptography breaks or some other tography breaks. it’ll be ok

unlike many other professions, people who aren’t coders and mathematicians have no idea what coders and mathematicians actually do

when someone is a photographer, other people understand what the photographer does even if they aren’t photographers. they have a rough idea of how it works, and even the meta properties of how the photography field as a whole works, how one becomes a famous photographer, etc

when an ai model figures out how to create photos, it’s actually devastating to the field of photography. the negative impact of that is imo very likely to be much greater than the hypothetical negative impact of any cryptographic assumption being broken

however since we all have an intuitive understanding of the field of photography even if we’re not experts, the theoretical impact, as significant as it is, is BOUNDED. we all know what the worst case is. so while actual photographers are losing their shit, the rest of us generally moved on

coders and math heads aren’t like that, 99% of folks have no idea what those people do. everybody uses cryptography every day yet no one has any idea how it works. therefore the hypothetical impact, in the average person’s mind, is unbounded

are planes going to fall off the sky? will nuclear codes leak leading to atomic bombs going off in major cities? will all bank accounts zero out? well… why not?

the people whose job it is to calm people down are too preoccupied in the same existential crisis photographers already went through. they’re too busy asking themselves “who am i” to consider that planes aren’t going to fall out of the sky actually

————

if it makes you feel better: cryptography is a tool. society does not run on cryptography. society runs on humans. and humans figure shit out. even if photography breaks or cryptography breaks or some other tography breaks. it’ll be ok

$HPE CEO: "We expect supply of memory, NAND, and many other critical components to remain constrained to at least H2 2028."

$DELL Vice Chairman: "there’s nothing that suggests that we're going to see price declines in enterprise NAND and DRAM for servers."

JP Morgan note: 

- Per OpenRouter, overall token spend continued to increase (+8% M/M growth), while volume pricing declined -39% M/M. 

- A100 GPU prices increased, H100 and B200 prices also continued to increase M/M

- DRAM price gains moderated, while NAND spot declined. 

On the latter part, I covered China selling inventory on NAND/eSSD spot markets. This was procurement delays around $NVDA GPUs/DRAM shortages, demand to re-accelerate after component arrive. (source Phison CEO)

Enterprise NAND pricing might see different rates than spot markets, as seen with Dell Chairman comments. 

TLDR: 
- Token spend continues to grow despite users shifting to cheaper Chinese models
- Bullish comments on DRAM duration (also seen with $AMBA earnings), but consumer demand weakening
- Compute pricing continues to increase in November
-  More nuanced for NAND, weakness in near term NAND spot markets (with expected rebound after GPUs/DRAM/components arrive), enterprise NAND markets seem resilient.

I think most of the major AI names are close to full mean reversions with respect to their 1D 200 SMAs. Indicies I believe have more room to drop but most likely >50% through their corrections.

Equity bear markets are usually mean reverting and provide multiple relief rallies before they find a bottom which is not the case with current price action.

This looks to be a liquidity contraction driving the mean reversion. DXY rising whilst every other asset is being sold for cash. When policy becomes too restrictive this is what happens.

Concerns are shifting from inflation which is cooling towards growth. Copper selling off is one of the indications of a growth scare. We do not have covid level inflation that is a result of fiscal stimulus. We do have inflationary forces from energy and also the AI infrastructure build out. 

It's my expectation that inflation cools in 2027 and the FED moves away from restrictive policy towards easing where we would finally have a positive outlook with respect to improving liquidity conditions. 

I think the AI names here and any remaining downside are now value.

$ELEF.TO $SILEF #Germanium #Zinc #CriticalMinerals #Silver

One Kentucky core sample was 50.17% zinc. The reason I’m bullish is what came with it: 115.4 g/t germanium. Roughly 760 metres away, a spot sample from another hole returned 215.4 g/t germanium, 40.57% zinc and 23.2 g/t silver.

Why could that be valuable? Germanium goes into fiber-optic networks and infrared optics, and most of it is already recovered as a byproduct of zinc processing. Silver Elephant cites a germanium price of $269/oz. If enough of it follows the zinc into concentrate and a refiner pays for it, the company could earn more from the same tonnes it mines and mills. That’s the upside I see at Robinson-Lasher.

Now for the two numbers I want to see: grade across a full interval and percentage recovered into concentrate. These were spot samples, and a hole between the two carried little germanium. With 232 historical drill holes to guide follow-up, Silver Elephant has plenty to work with.

I came for the Bolivian silver. A potential U.S. source of germanium gives me a reason to watch the Kentucky drill results just as closely.

very much agree with Felipe here.

look, I get it. the last 5 years were horrible in terms of price action, especially compared to what we were used to before.

but these are just the natural cycles every emerging technology goes through:

irruption → frenzy → turning point (we are here) → synergy → maturity.

the first 15 years of crypto were full of utopian dreams, big promises and delusional experiments, and as a result, massive overspeculation.

and that's fine. it's part of the game, and gg to everyone who caught that wave early and played it right.

but times have changed.

like every emerging tech industry before us, we're now at the turning point. the frenzy is over. you can't raise a billion dollars on a whitepaper and empty promises anymore.

that's a good thing btw lol.

it's time to deliver. time to grow into the massive promises we made, and into the inflated valuations we created (which have come down a lot, and that only works in our favor).

most emerging industries die right here, because this is the hardest step: bridging the gap to the golden age of deployment and mainstream adoption.

I'm very confident we're near the end of that gap. we won't just survive it. as Felipe says, we have a golden age and a secular bull decade ahead of us.

never before have we had so many great onchain businesses with real product market fit and billions in revenue, because we finally built things people actually want. as an industry we're doubling down on what works (finance), and it's working.

never before have we had so many politicians waking up to how important this technology is, instead of running a witch hunt against us.

never before have we had so many institutions investing in our industry, or adopting the tech and building onchain themselves, simply because it's better for their business.

and most importantly, never before have we had such a clear view of the mistakes we made and what we need to do from here. it may look like a few random degens on the timeline haven't learned anything, but the smartest and most influential people in this industry are very aware of the problems and working hard to fix them.

I know it feels tough right now, and I get it. it's not easy and it's not fun. but we've been here before. as long as we don't lose our belief and stay focused on what we actually have to deliver, the golden age is inevitable.

it might sound cheesy, but sometimes it really is darkest before the dawn. don't let your emotions stand between you and what could be one of the greatest opportunities of your lifetime.

the fact that you're still here and reading this already puts you among the winners of what's coming.

so make the most of it.

I know it feels tough right now, and I get it. it's not easy and it's not fun. but we've been here before. as long as we don't lose our belief and stay focused on what we actually have to deliver, the golden age is inevitable.

it might sound cheesy, but sometimes it really is darkest before the dawn. don't let your emotions stand between you and what could be one of the greatest opportunities of your lifetime.

the fact that you're still here and reading this already puts you among the winners of what's coming.

so make the most of it.

As you guys know I only talk about a specific trade once in a blue moon, but I'm heavily convicted on a Risk/Reward setup here so will share.

NFA, this is just my own thoughts. 

For the past few months I have been doing a deep dive into finding the best ways to invest into the AI trade as it continues to transform the economy. 

Have looked extensively at the range of both public and private opportunities. I think there will be very good high yield opportunities on the privates side that can be done at size, and will look to source these and possibly bring them onchain. 

But in the meantime with the recent huge dislocations in prices, I think the greatest R/R opportunity is on the public side, specifically in @nebiusai $NBIS. 

At the time of this post its at $76-77, anything under $80 with a first target of ~$120 feels like one of the best +50% setups I have seen that can be done in size in a very long time. 

The funding of the AI capex buildout has understandably shaken the market up, as the circular economics are sometimes hard to untangle properly. This combined with Nebius having a delay on one of their sites took the wind out of the stock, which was trading at $160 just a couple weeks ago.

I can write an entire book as a thesis but to keep it very short- There are several advantages Nebius has that made me choose it for this trade:

-The balance sheet is extremely robust for a neocloud and their conservative fiscal approach will help them survive this liquidity airgap.
-Their technical ability on delivering capacity and operating it is extremely high, making them a preferred partners of the major players like NVIDIA, Databrick etc. 
-This also has allowed them to develop scalable business lines like their asset-light model where someone else funds the buildout. The Asset-Light model is already generating huge returns and is underpriced for now as it isn't marked as 'ARR'.
-They have other great assets on the Balance sheet including a very valuable 25% stake in Clickhouse that create even more surface area for things to go well.

There's a lot more for those who want to research more deeply- And while anything is possible in these crazy times, in my estimation this R/R sits at the highest point of  'AI Capex Mountain' -- if the floodwater is going to reach that high then the entire AI sector is cooked anyway.

Timing wise for the 50+% bounce, at this point for it to happen quickly will likely require a liquidity injection of some sort. I don't think we are too far from something like that being needed, though of course it might mean things get worse before they get better so I wouldn't have leverage on at this time. 

Within 6 months I am expecting this to trade a LOT higher and am personally positioning accordingly. Sharing for entertainment purposes only, I know most of us already are deployed and not much in cash so stay safe out there.

As you guys know I only talk about a specific trade once in a blue moon, but I'm heavily convicted on a Risk/Reward setup here so will share.

NFA, this is just my own thoughts. 

For the past few months I have been doing a deep dive into finding the best ways to invest into the AI trade as it continues to transform the economy. 

Have looked extensively at the range of both public and private opportunities. I think there will be very good high yield opportunities on the privates side that can be done at size, and will look to source these and possibly bring them onchain. 

But in the meantime with the recent huge dislocations in prices, I think the greatest R/R opportunity is on the public side, specifically in @nebiusai $NBIS. 

At the time of this post its at $76-77, anything under $80 with a first target of ~$120 feels like one of the best +50% setups I have seen that can be done in size in a very long time. 

The funding of the AI capex buildout has understandably shaken the market up, as the circular economics are sometimes hard to untangle properly. This combined with Nebius having a delay on one of their sites took the wind out of the stock, which was trading at $160 just a couple weeks ago.

I can write an entire book as a thesis but to keep it very short- There are several advantages Nebius has that made me choose it for this trade:

-The balance sheet is extremely robust for a neocloud and their conservative fiscal approach will help them survive this liquidity airgap.
-Their technical ability on delivering capacity and operating it is extremely high, making them a preferred partners of the major players like NVIDIA, Databrick etc. 
-This also has allowed them to develop scalable business lines like their asset-light model where someone else funds the buildout. The Asset-Light model is already generating huge returns and is underpriced for now as it isn't marked as 'ARR'.
-They have other great assets on the Balance sheet including a very valuable 25% stake in Clickhouse that create even more surface area for things to go well.

There's a lot more for those who want to research more deeply- And while anything is possible in these crazy times, in my estimation this R/R sits at the highest point of  'AI Capex Mountain' -- if the floodwater is going to reach that high then the entire AI sector is cooked anyway.

Timing wise for the 50+% bounce, at this point for it to happen quickly will likely require a liquidity injection of some sort. I don't think we are too far from something like that being needed, though of course it might mean things get worse before they get better so I wouldn't have leverage on at this time. 

Within 6 months I am expecting this to trade a LOT higher and am personally positioning accordingly. Sharing for entertainment purposes only, I know most of us already are deployed and not much in cash so stay safe out there.

tweets.text:
“Infrastructure demand continues to outpace supply. As we look into next year, the gap between component supply and end user demand continues to widen...In fact, we think the demand is further ahead of supply in calendar ‘27 than it’s been in ‘26” so said Dell yesterday on their call but the market doesn’t believe them and likely why their big beat and raise is not being rewarded.

Why? There is compute capacity supply coming and it’s coming from Asia as data centers there powered by US tech are about to lose China as a customer. In a Bloomberg News article today, “Data centers across Asia are racing to offload excess computing power to US buyers after the Trump administration tightened a loophole that gave Chinese tech firms access to Nvidia’s most advanced chips. That’s according to Ronit Jain, chief executive and co-founder of Liquid Compute, a New York based startup building a regulated exchange for AI computing capacity.”

“The cost to access Nvidia’s powerful B300 graphics processing units was $7.72 per GPU hour at the end of last month, according to a Liquid Compute index. That had fallen 7% to $7.19 as of Tuesday, according to the startup, which says it tracks over 200 data center companies.”

“A post Jain made on X last week highlighting the declining prices drew widespread attention.

‘All the neoclouds based in Asia-Pacific selling to Tencent and other companies, or in Singapore or Taiwan with Chinese companies as offtakers, have excess capacity,’ Jain said in an interview. ‘They’re trying to broker it into the US.’ He declined to name the companies selling their excess compute, or the buyers.”

Computing capacity doesn’t have geographic boundaries and we need to think globally about this with the debate over the supply and demand of it.
@ronitrjain

Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".

Three primary reasons:

1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and ETH function in ways that are very hard to make compatible with decentralization and capture resistance.
3. Meanwhile, optimizing for ETH as SoV is aligned with Ethereum focusing on its unique strengths (decentralization and CROPS)

EIP-1559 (including its burn) is fine and good, we should keep them. But we should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.

The core idea: the big thing that people appreciate about Ethereum is decentralization and CROPS. The main pragmatic benefit that these things translate into is stability. SoV is the category where that is not an unneeded extra we merely put effort into for ideological reasons, but rather a pragmatic strength from the perspective of people putting in their assets. And in the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued.

Hold the line.

“Maybe you can't be short, I don't know, because things could still rip in your face.

But it's hard to justify how you get super long here.

The valuation of Anthropic over the next three or four months has mostly nothing to do with Anthropic.

If you look at other businesses that are making gobs of money, NVIDIA's a perfect example, we've never seen a quarter like this, ever, and the stock is down.

Why is that? Right now, what it looks like is (the market) is trying to will itself to go up, and the problem is that inflation is sticky, and all of these external conditions are not resolved, including the war.

I think people, on balance, feel skittish. They feel like this has run for a while, and I think the balance of trade is to de-risk, not to add more risk.

So I think you're going to have all kinds of pockets of opportunities to buy stuff much cheaper.

What I do know is that the 10-year unfortunately keeps ticking up. That's bad for equities.

Vol is a little bit elevated. That's bad for equities.

Inflation is sticky. That's bad for equities.

To the extent Kevin Warsh wanted to cut, I don't think he's got much room, and if anything, he's going to hike. That's bad for equities.

There's a new sheriff in town in the Senate and in Congress. That creates uncertainty. That's bad for equities.”

$ANT $NVDA

This principle means that every meeting should have a responsible party whose goals define its purpose, but that responsibility does not mean one‑sided service. 

The meeting serves the responsible person’s objectives while also serving the participants by providing them with useful information or decisions; a “no” can be a valid answer if it aligns with those objectives, yet the leader must still listen, explain, and seek alignment. 

In practice, you might say: “I’m running this meeting to decide on X; I need your input, but if we can’t agree, we’ll document the disagreement and move forward.” This balances direction with two‑way service.

Agents started on the 25th November last year. They now exceed all human users on the internet.

That won't surprise a lot of you. Everyone on here has one agent tracking their protein intake, another summarising the newsletters they were never going to read, another replying to emails that someone else's agent wrote, and a head honcho to manage them all.

But step outside this incestuous echo chamber we call X for a second and think about the people you know in real life... (people who work in tech or crypto don't count) Your parents, your neighbours, the friends you grew up with. How many of them use agents? In the US its fewer than one in 10.

It's the iPhone in its first year. Apple sold around 6 million of them, so you probably didnt know anyone who had one, and now almost everyone you know has a smartphone in their pocket. Agents will go the same way... except the iPhone didnt take over half the internet while it was still in a few million hands.

That 57% is coming from a tiny group of early users. As adoption increases, which it inevitably will, the volume will explode beyond anything we can comprehend.

And every one of those agents has to pay for things. Data, compute, the work of other agents, often a cent or less at a time. All of that will happen onchain.

That changes the maths on crypto completely. Every adoption forecast added up the humans who might one day use it. But humans are about to be the minority of users, the same way they're already the minority of the internet... 

Trillions of agents will transact onchain. More times in a minute than you do in a month.

tweets.text:
Cross-asset sentiment peaked on April 30th.

From there, the S&P 500 rallied another 8.5% to its October record... and has since given all of it back. It's now slightly below where it was on the day of the peak.

That's the typical pattern.

After euphoric peaks since 1990, the S&P 500 was up just 1.1% a year later on average. At all other times, 11.8%. After capitulations, 20.7%.

Bitcoin was lower a year later every single time, with the median low coming about nine months in.

The euphoria tax is being paid. So far Bitcoin and the AI trade have paid most of the bill, while the S&P has gone sideways.

Who pays next, and when does it turn?

That's the question for 2027.

The full story is in The 2027 Macro Outlook, out Friday.

Not gonna lie, it's been brutal since the October high. Some current thoughts on price action. 

Crypto lows tend to form in capitulation, near the low in global liquidity. In 2022 it was two capitulations with the second one hitting with less force than the first; a bullish divergence.

That's why I thought June was the low. Bitcoin formed a typically v reliable bullish divergence on the weekly RSI btwn Feb and June lows. While, the broader Top 200 index gave similiar divergences on RSI and 365-day lows. 

However, I have been consistent on what would invalidate my thesis. The one thing that was hanging over the market's head like an anvil: global liquidity, which was still deteriorating and hadn't bottomed. If the cadence of the past holds, expect that trough by around mid 2027. I think sooner (Q1).

But I don't think it gets anywhere near as deep as past ones. This cycle's liquidity high was far more muted after the excess of the 2020 Covid-calamity response. They also shifted it from the Fed to the Treasury. Differnece mechanism of action. Different winners. However, with debt outstanding so much higher than in past cycles, governments have ever-diminishing capacity to tolerate deflating asset prices. That may be hopium, but it's my read.

So, a very uncomfortable few weeks, maybe months, before this resolves. On many technical measures, in tech and crypto, exhaustion levels are being hit. That doesn't mean we can't go lower. The Nasdaq 100 fell almost 20% into last week's low, and I think 30% to 35% is the worst case before authorities step in. We'll have to wait and see.

I think crypto has been in a funk for five years, and the Top 200 is still 42% below its Nov 2021 high. But my quality basket is up 16% YTD. I suspect the market is starting to work out crypto fundamentals, or crypto protocols are starting to behave more responsibly. Likely both, and either way an overdue sign of maturity for an asset class that has pissed away a tonne of goodwill. 

5 years of broad bear market is about how long the first hype-bust wave of a new technology usually takes, but it's no longer hype. This is the infrastructure global finance is being rebuilt on.

The companies leaning hardest into blockchain and AI will win, and tokens with real quality attributes (product-market fit, strong value accrual) and low or negative inflation are where I think the outsized gains will come from. The reality is that the gap between now and then is uncomfortable for holders, like me, but it's going to be an amazing opportunity.

What I'm watching into next year: visible action from Bitcoin on quantum, where signs are emerging. Tokenised stocks, which I think will likely have doubled by early next year. And on-chain trading activity, which DEX token prices track closely.

Last word is that I have always said owning Bitcoin is like playing chicken with the central planners. Strap in if you are still here for the ride.

thread_tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
Bitcoin does not have a security incentive issue

The only people who talk about this as a main concern are non-Bitcoiners. I watch and read a lot of content and the incentive security thing is not something Bitcoiners worry about because it's fundamentally in the premise of Bitcoin. Yet every time some non-Bitcoiner argues this is all they talk about lol. They do so because from first principles they have come to realise that every other argument against Bitcoin is proving not viable and it's the only thing that's "in the future" that they can knock.

People get stuck on this idea of "bitcoin cant double every 4 yrs to keep incentives for miners and wont be able to rely on fees in decades ahead"

1)You are thinking in fiat terms - there is no reason why it cant nominally on a fiat denominator although it does not need to
2)When fiat becomes increasingly worthless like in many countries the Bitcoin chart is parabolic on parabolic in that currency - the issue is even thinking from fiat view for security long term
3)Long term when your currency goes through very high inflation you are just going to want the Bitcoin - as a thought experiment how much Burmese kiat are you willing to sell Bitcoin for?
4)Bitcoin has gone through multiple 70% declines and had no issues as hashrate readjusts 
5)Miners will continue to search and find more effective ways to mine from equipment to energy costs ie Moores Law
6)In gaining adoption and usage across multiple layers in the long term there is various ways that an increase in fees will also come to bare and a purely fee based incentine is not for over 100 yrs
7)Many new market dynamics we cant even conceive will happen ie if fiat is worthless why wouldnt every country try to mine Bitcoin and acquire at any cost

You cannot understand Bitcoin and think it has a security issue - it goes hand and hand with the premise of Bitcoin - "Bitcoin has a security issues" just means "I dont believe in Bitcoin"

So if you own Bitcoin but believe there is a security issue you need to reduce your exposure because it means you only see the speculation of it and large downside volatility will haunt you as you wont be able to face your thinking based on logic but emotion

#bitcoin

thread_tweets.text: @mackerjer https://x.com/0x_kun/status/1913880250087514602
thread_tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
From first principles what Bitcoin needs over time is more hash rate - people mistakenly think in the derivative of this by saying “Bitcoin needs to double every 4 years for the security incentive”

That’s a false premise and two different things

Firstly there are multiple reasons hash rate can increase:

-More efficient equipment

-Finding cheaper sources of energy

-Incentives to acquire Bitcoin outside of just market buying

Second hash rate adjusts over time to manage incentives - the same way higher interest rates incentivise demand for Treasuries. A drop in hash rate invites miners who are profitable at different thresholds to come online

Third Bitcoin doesn’t need to double from its previous ATH every 4 years. What it needs is a general upward trend that reflects the cost of energy/mining - which is currently thought in fiat generally USD but not always the case - Reread this point - Reflects cost of energy over time not the fiat quote.

Example: When Bitcoin hit 69k the avg mining cost in USD was ~22k. Four years later post-halving 44k would still be profitable for those same miners had nothing changed and that’s just the average. Some miners have lower, some higher than average and this is not static but a constant motion

If you look at mining cost trends they’ve steadily doubled every four years in USD anyway and even though that’s not required (as mentioned in the points above) it kills the argument and shows a large flaw in the "well it hasnt doubled since 69k" - those miners just got to make a tonne more at that arbitrage but nonetheless profitable and its times like that like the volatility in markets for normal buyers that allows miners to make risk adjusted returns 

And finally, when price rips 3-4x above the avg mining cost, miners sell or bring more rigs online to rebalance and its the short term speculators who are impacted. On the flip side when China banned mining and hash rate dropped, it opened the door for new growth elsewhere and within a year, the hash rate was higher than ever.

One of my favourite things about Bitcoin which is not discussed in most Bitcoin circles as much is this equilibrium function which works on many levels but particularly

1)A shared ethical basis for money where no participant acquires money at a preferential rate risk adjusted
2)That without talking about fiat what its done is tie itself to energy/hardware - hence just the random fiat quote is not the basis for security

If and when the quote is BTC itself (although also does not need to be the case) people will just want BTC because its BTC -  it will be acquired as the end goal it will be like us thinking now about if we could mine USD.
This does not work with gold because even if the quote is in gold - noone can take gold for goods and services due to divisibility and portability issues and needs to then be once removed via some sort of issued paper.

There are many ways to discuss this topic and have never been bothered to as Ive thought this was base level bitcoin understanding but ive figured that with the number of people talking about security cost in the Bitcoin skeptic camps its worth sharing to help increase understanding.
This is the same as when I didnt tweet about investing but then realised basic concepts like "starting from view you could be wrong" was game changing for lot of people.

tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
OpenAI has posted their own VP ≠ VNP proof in response to Anthropic's, and says their result 'was obtained on November 6, 2026.' Two weeks ago. The ETH papers were also released in an similar oneupmanship fashion. As with Anthropic's result, no name on the paper (my guess is this was GPT-Aeon). Also like Anthropic: no announcement, no blog post, no tweet. 

This is a significant result, yet both OpenAI and Anthropic chose to simply dump it online with no comment. I was listening to a Scott Aaronson interview this morning where he said this specific result would update him toward 'a solution to P ≠ NP by the AIs might really be around the corner.'
To me this is more evidence for my argument that both OpenAI and Anthropic are sitting on a dragon's hoard of scientific results they are not releasing to the public. The first massive 700+ paper OpenAI GitHub dump took five weeks for their model to generate. It's been seven weeks since then, and their internal model has continued to improve. They said they had it working on 4,000 problems. How many have been solved in the last seven weeks? Based on the last release, 1,000+ is not unreasonable.

I will quote OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki from the blog post 'Perplexity and Intelligence,' posted 48 hours ago:

'We have recently witnessed unprecedented acceleration in another domain. For more than a year, we have been posing open problems in mathematics to our models as one of the ways of evaluating them. Once we upgraded to a model of log-perplexity ~0.76, it started producing groundbreaking results. For many of us that have previously worked in mathematics and adjacent fields, seeing the resolutions to questions we've long thought about coming out of the model one after another in a single Slack thread felt deeply surreal.'

There have also been, of late, multiple rumors about breakthroughs in cryptography that I have been reluctant to post about for obvious reasons. Specifically, there have been rumors of an encryption breakthrough at Anthropic. What I personally took from the big OpenAI math release was that all encryption will be cracked much sooner than people are expecting, and that the rate of scientific discoveries will continually increase as we continue to scale up. No, not will increase, *has increased*. At both labs. We just don't know about it yet. Because unless you work at those labs, the current frontier is completely invisible. But it won't stay that way forever. Or to put it another way: prepare yourself for revelations.
